subject.title: #94249: skill_workshop apply times out on large proposals (~28KB)

question: Should Skill Workshop lifecycle approvals keep the current 70s watchdog-aligned timeout, or should OpenClaw pursue a longer/configurable approval window with matching Codex watchdog changes?
rationale: The choice changes both availability behavior and the lifetime of an approval for generated skill content, so automation should not pick the permanent timeout policy.

options.title: Keep current bounded timeout
options.body: Treat the current 70s main behavior as the chosen fail-closed contract and ask this stale PR to close or rebase away the 300s override.

options.title: Sponsor longer approvals
options.body: Require a maintainer-owned redesign that aligns every outer watchdog, adds tests, and provides live approval-path proof before a longer approval window lands.

options.title: Defer to approval UX work
options.body: Keep the longer-TTL request out of this PR and handle async operator needs through a broader approval UX/config decision.

recommendation.title: Keep current bounded timeout
recommendation.body: Treat the current 70s main behavior as the chosen fail-closed contract and ask this stale PR to close or rebase away the 300s override.

likelyOwner.reason: Current main's timeout-aligned Skill Workshop policy and adjacent Codex dynamic-tool work point here as the best available owner for the timeout/security choice.
